items.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018
items.q: But I took that for myself. And it made me able to accept people not understanding what I was trying to write or form as musical.

ctx.x: Outside stimulus meaning someone else has written down what they want you to do, either real specifically or just in a framework.

Yeah. Yeah. Well see now even people like John Cage for instance, definitely had a framework. But he wanted you to infuse your ideas into that framework. And I remember oh man, it was really weird. We were in the University of Illinois and Cage was there one day. And you know you’re playing all this weird music, and some of it was written you know but he’d tell you to do something, and I did something unusual and I’m looking at him down there at his seat. And I did it. And he like had an orgasm, like that, some…

So I’ve been thinking about this, I watched a few things on YouTube that you were on, and then some other things that Joseph Daley had done. I was trying to surmise if listening to avante garde or free or extremely creative music is easier for people who don’t know how music works? Because I think I have a bad habit of trying to compartmentalize things if I’m listening to something, and I’m listening — okay I’ve got the groove or I can hear the key, I can hear the root. And then if music comes along that it’s not…
